home-server-source.description: GitHub Secret HOME_SERVER_ENV before deploy-time image injection.

keys.name: API_DOMAIN
keys.description: Host-based API vhost address in the Caddyfile. Since #1575 the public API is same-origin under WEB_DOMAIN, so this is no longer the public API host and no longer the topology switch (CUSTOM_PROD_BACKURL is). It keeps the pre-transition host reachable while the old web origin is still served; retiring that host removes this key and its address, but not the vhost, which also carries the permanent container-internal entry point http://caddy (#1539). It may never equal WEB_DOMAIN: two Caddy site blocks sharing one address take the whole edge down on the next caddy recreate.

keys.name: LEGACY_API_DOMAIN
keys.description: Transition-only second site address for the API vhost, so the old and the new public API host are both reachable during the domain cutover. Unset outside that window. Deliberately NOT part of cookieDomainScope.topologies: it is the host the transition is moving away from, so the topology invariants do not apply to it.
keys.warnWhenPresent: the domain cutover window is open: the old public API host is still served. Remove LEGACY_API_DOMAIN (and its DNS/Tunnel hostname) once the new host is verified. The #1575 same-origin cutover does not use this key - the old API host it leaves behind is API_DOMAIN itself, and that address stays. Close the window by DELETING the line: an empty value is not the same as an unset one and drops the API host matcher entirely.

keys.name: WEB_DOMAIN
keys.description: Public web host served by the Caddy web vhost (#1538). Since #1575 it also carries the public API paths, so it is the host the auth cookie is scoped to. Optional only before the cutover: once CUSTOM_PROD_BACKURL moves to the same-origin topology, leaving this unset would 404 the public site AND the public API while the contract still passed. Colliding with API_DOMAIN would duplicate a Caddy site address and take the whole edge down on the next caddy recreate.

keys.name: COMPANY_DOMAIN
keys.description: Company surface host served by its own Caddy vhost from the same front container (#1605). It is the site canonical, and APEX_DOMAIN's redirect target is derived from this key. Optional: while unset the vhost stays on its unreachable company.localhost default, which is the shape that keeps the surface invisible until the owner opens its Tunnel hostname. An empty value means nothing here - it collapses the site address to `http://`, a host-matcher-less :80 catch-all - so it is rejected outright. Pinned to one host like API_DOMAIN, because the front does not learn this value at runtime: front/site.config.js hard-codes the surface canonical table and src/libs/publicSurfaceUrl.ts matches the request Host against it. Any other hostname would be served by Caddy while canonical/OG pointed elsewhere and the sitemap host guard rejected it - a silent metadata mismatch instead of a rejected config.

keys.name: PRODUCT_DOMAIN
keys.description: Product surface host served by its own Caddy vhost from the same front container (#1605). Same optional-but-never-empty rule as COMPANY_DOMAIN, and pinned to one host for the same reason: the front's surface canonical table is compiled in, not injected.

keys.name: APEX_DOMAIN
keys.description: Apex host whose vhost 308s to COMPANY_DOMAIN with path and query preserved (#1605). It serves no content of its own. Same optional-but-never-empty rule as COMPANY_DOMAIN; setting it without COMPANY_DOMAIN would redirect the apex at the unreachable company.localhost default, so the cross-check below requires the pair.

keys.name: WEB_UPSTREAM
keys.description: Active front colour the Caddy web vhost proxies to (default front_blue). Interpolated straight into the Caddyfile reverse_proxy target, so a typo would route public web traffic at whatever else Caddy can reach. The blue/green switch that writes it is #1539.

keys.name: BACKEND_INTERNAL_URL
keys.description: Compose-internal API entry point the front server side uses (SSR helpers and the /api/backend/* proxy). Pinned to the Caddy internal address (#1539) because it is the only value that stays correct: a blue/green colour URL breaks on every backend cutover, and back_read/back_admin answer 503 outside their runtime mode (ApiRuntimeBoundaryFilter), so neither can serve both the public feed and the auth/write paths. front/src/libs/server/backend.ts throws in production when it is missing while the container still reports healthy, because the healthcheck only serves a static file. Public internet must not be traversed here.

keys.name: PROD___SPRING__FLYWAY__USER
keys.description: Dedicated Flyway migration role. Must not be postgres superuser (#1131).

keys.name: PROD___SPRING__FLYWAY__PASSWORD
keys.description: Required dedicated Flyway password. No PROD___POSTGRES__PASSWORD fallback (#1131).

keys.name: PROD___POSTGRES_EXPORTER__USERNAME
keys.description: Dedicated postgres_exporter role (default postgres_exporter). Must not be postgres.

keys.name: PROD___POSTGRES_EXPORTER__PASSWORD
keys.description: Password for pg_monitor exporter role. Never reuse the postgres superuser password in docs.

keys.name: CUSTOM_PROD_BACKURL
keys.description: Public API origin AND the single switch for the prod site topology (#1575). allowedHosts is a second, independent edit point: without it the accepted switch values were defined by cookieDomainScope.topologies alone, so adding a table entry silently widened what the switch accepts. Compared by HOST, not raw string - every other layer of this contract compares hosts, and a raw allowedValues would make a trailing slash a rejection reason here while the topology check accepted it.

keys.name: CUSTOM__REVALIDATE__URL
keys.warnWhenAbsent: post write/modify/delete events enqueue revalidate tasks (RevalidateEventListener) that RevalidateService drops silently while this is empty, so published posts only appear after the 1h ISR window. Set it once the front tier runs on the homeserver (#1538).

keys.name: CUSTOM__REVALIDATE__TOKEN
keys.warnWhenAbsent: RevalidateService also drops every task when this is empty, even if CUSTOM__REVALIDATE__URL is set.

keys.name: CUSTOM_STORAGE_KEYPREFIX
keys.description: Post object-key prefix (default posts). Must be non-blank when set; mutually exclusive with CUSTOM_STORAGE_CLOUD_KEY_PREFIX (no equality or path containment such as posts vs posts/images). Backend fails fast on blank/overlap.

keys.name: CUSTOM_STORAGE_CLOUD_KEY_PREFIX
keys.description: Cloud object-key prefix (default cloud). Must be non-blank when set; mutually exclusive with CUSTOM_STORAGE_KEYPREFIX (no equality or path containment). Backend fails fast on blank/overlap.

crossChecks.description: Every one of these keys is interpolated into a Caddy site address. Two site blocks sharing one address is not a routing mistake that shows up as a 404 - caddy fails to start and the whole edge goes down on the next recreate. mustDifferFrom is pairwise and cannot close a set, so the set is checked here. Comparison is by normalized host, because a duplicate spelled with different case is still the same address to Caddy.

The apex vhost's redirect target is {$COMPANY_DOMAIN}. With APEX_DOMAIN set and COMPANY_DOMAIN unset, the apex would 308 every visitor to the unreachable company.localhost default - a live public host pointing at nothing, which reads as a working redirect in the config and as a dead site to the visitor.

The auth cookie Domain is the front/back shared suffix, so every front-derived value must move together. There is no separate urlHostEquals(CUSTOM_PROD_BACKURL, WEB_DOMAIN) check because it would be false in the legacy topology; the same-origin pairing is closed transitively instead - the switch selects the topology, CUSTOM_PROD_FRONTURL must equal its frontHost (error), and urlHostEquals(CUSTOM_PROD_FRONTURL, WEB_DOMAIN) pins WEB_DOMAIN to that host (error), while requiredWhen makes WEB_DOMAIN mandatory the moment the switch reaches the same-origin host. CUSTOM_PROD_BACKURL is the single switch: its HOST selects one declared topology, and the other values are compared against that topology by host (not by raw spelling, because HOME_SERVER_ENV values can differ in trailing slash or case). It replaced API_DOMAIN as the switch in #1575, when the public API moved onto the web host by path - API_DOMAIN is now only the Caddy host-based API vhost address and must differ from WEB_DOMAIN, so it can no longer name the public API. deploy.yml pins the same table. The table itself is checked against the invariants below, so a wrong table entry cannot pass by simply matching.

invariants.description: Enforced against EVERY declared topology, not just the selected one, so a wrong table entry cannot hide until the switch flips. cookieDomain must be the web host itself, and the public API must either BE that web host (same-origin, the #1575 target) or sit strictly under it; otherwise the front/back shared suffix climbs one level and session cookies reach hosts this blog does not own. forbiddenCookieDomains names the hosts another service owns. legacyUnsafeTopology is the single entry allowed to violate these, and it must carry structurallyUnsafe: true.

api.aquilaxk.site.warn: pre-transition domain set: the cookie Domain is the apex, which another service owns. Update HOME_SERVER_ENV CUSTOM_PROD_BACKURL to https://blog.aquilaxk.site (and WEB_DOMAIN to blog.aquilaxk.site) to activate the same-origin blog domain contract (#1575)

keys.name: FRONT_BLUE_IMAGE
keys.description: Front runtime image for the blue colour (#1538). Digest only; ghcr.io/<owner>/<repo>-front tags are rejected. Optional until #1539 injects it, and the compose front profile stays off while it is empty.

keys.name: FRONT_GREEN_IMAGE
keys.description: Front runtime image for the green colour (#1538). Same digest-only rule as FRONT_BLUE_IMAGE.
